open_points.subject: HTTP header framing validation
open_points.text: a request whose `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding` header is malformed
open_points.question: Exactly which header forms are malformed, including repeated or conflicting `Content-Length`, simultaneous `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, unsupported transfer codings, coding lists, overflow and non-canonical numeric forms?
options: Accept only one canonical `Content-Length` or exactly `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and reject every conflict or unsupported coding
Delegate all validity decisions to the HTTP library
Accept every form the applicable HTTP version permits
open_points.default_guess: Accept one valid `Content-Length` or exactly chunked transfer encoding, reject both together, reject conflicting duplicates and unsupported codings.

open_points.subject: malformed-header refusal
open_points.text: is refused by the listener from its headers alone, its connection closed, and reaches no surface
open_points.question: Before closing the connection, does the listener send an HTTP error response, and if so which status and response shape, or does it close without an answer?
options: Send a fixed HTTP error and then close
Close without sending an HTTP response
Use whatever response the HTTP library produces
open_points.default_guess: Send a minimal 400 response when safely possible, then close.

witness.initial: A client has connected and sends a syntactically invalid `Content-Length` header.
events: The client completes the header block.
The listener detects the malformed header.
outcomes: The client receives an HTTP 400 response and then EOF.
The client receives EOF or a reset without any HTTP response.
witness.observer: The calling client and any monitor classifying HTTP responses

open_points.subject: body-framing stream failure
open_points.text: whose chunks are malformed, is a failure of the stream its reader sees while reading it
open_points.question: Which module owns the stream-failure type and its handling: `instance_lifecycle`, the reading `service_api` or `owner_interface` module, or another transport abstraction, and in which direction does that dependency run?
options: `instance_lifecycle` owns the framed stream and catches its failure around each surface invocation
Each surface imports and handles a transport failure exported by `instance_lifecycle`
A separate HTTP transport module owns the stream contract and is known by lifecycle and both surfaces
open_points.default_guess: Keep the transport failure private to `instance_lifecycle`; invoke a surface under a wrapper that catches the failure and terminates the request and connection.

open_points.subject: operation outcome after a body-framing failure
open_points.text: a body that ends before its framing says, or whose chunks are malformed, is a failure of the stream its reader sees while reading it
open_points.question: What is the operation-level outcome when this failure occurs after the request has reached a surface: must the operation be treated as refused with no state change, may already completed checks or session changes remain, and may an HTTP answer be sent?
options: The domain operation never begins until the complete required body is read; body failure changes no domain state and yields a fixed transport error
Checks and temporary session effects performed before the read failure remain, but no durable domain transaction commits
A streaming operation may retain effects committed before the failure
open_points.default_guess: Allow effects explicitly attached to request admission by earlier rules, but do not start or commit the domain operation until its complete inputs have been read; then send 400 if possible and close.

witness.initial: An authenticated owner request has a valid header block and begins a body whose declared framing is incomplete.
events: `owner_interface` accepts the session and starts reading form fields.
The body stream fails before all action inputs are available.
outcomes: The request is a transport failure; no operation runs, though admission effects required by the session rules remain.
The surface treats the partial request as an ordinary refused operation and applies a different set of session or confirmation effects.
witness.observer: The owner on the next request, and the store or audit-log reader

open_points.subject: connection disposition after body-stream failure
open_points.text: a body that ends before its framing says, or whose chunks are malformed, is a failure of the stream its reader sees while reading it
open_points.question: Must every body-stream framing failure close the connection, or may the listener attempt to recover and serve another request on it?
options: Always close the connection
Recover after a malformed chunk when a boundary can be found
Leave connection handling to the HTTP library
open_points.default_guess: Always close the connection because the next request boundary is no longer trustworthy.

witness.initial: A persistent connection carries a request with malformed chunk syntax followed by bytes intended as another request.
events: The surface reads until the framed stream reports failure.
The client waits to see whether the connection remains usable.
outcomes: The listener closes the connection and the client reconnects.
The listener attempts recovery and may accept another request on the same connection.
witness.observer: The client and the second requested surface

open_points.subject: unread request bodies
open_points.text: the body itself is never read ahead by the listener
open_points.question: When a surface answers without consuming the entire body, who disposes of the unread bytes, and is the connection drained, closed, or eligible for another request?
options: Close the connection whenever the surface leaves body bytes unread
Drain exactly the remaining framed body before reusing the connection
Require every surface to consume its stream fully before returning
open_points.default_guess: Close the connection when a surface returns with an unread body; do not drain it after the answer.

witness.initial: A request has valid framing and a large body, but authentication can be refused before the surface needs the body.
events: The surface returns the refusal without consuming the stream.
The client sends the remaining body bytes and then attempts another request on the same connection.
outcomes: The listener closes after the refusal, so the client must reconnect.
The listener drains the old body and reuses the connection for the next request.

open_points.subject: meaning of listener read-ahead
open_points.text: the body itself is never read ahead by the listener
open_points.question: Does “never read ahead” forbid only eager consumption before handing the stream to a surface, or also socket/library buffering and draining performed on demand after the surface returns?
options: It forbids only eager semantic consumption; ordinary bounded buffering is allowed
It forbids the listener from reading any body byte unless the surface requests it
It also forbids draining or buffering unread body bytes after the surface returns
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as forbidding eager semantic consumption while permitting bounded implementation buffering that is never exposed across the framed-body boundary.

open_points.subject: stalled framed bodies
open_points.question: What ends a request whose headers are valid but whose client neither completes nor terminates the body, and which module owns that timeout or cancellation?
options: No Registry body-read timeout; the request may remain blocked until the peer or host closes it
A release-fixed body-read timeout owned by `instance_lifecycle`
A timeout owned separately by each surface or its reader
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-fixed transport read timeout owned by `instance_lifecycle`, close the connection on expiry, and expose a stream failure to the reader.

witness.initial: A client declares a nonzero body or starts a chunk and keeps the connection open without sending the remaining bytes.
events: A surface waits on the handed-on body stream.
Minutes pass while the client sends nothing and does not disconnect.
outcomes: The request and its resources remain live indefinitely.
A transport timeout fails the stream and closes the connection.
witness.observer: The client and the operator observing occupied connections and request workers
